purpose: Freeze the conceptual provenance from Azami spatial phenotype mapping and EAzami evolutionary-history analysis to the aza3 Nature-scale evolvability question.

headline_patterns: floral_chroma x short-wave radiation survives biological reaggregation and full robustness sequence
presentation_angle x annual precipitation survives biological reaggregation and full robustness sequence

eazami.role: young-radiation history, recurrence, functional synthesis and historical-cause ceiling

conceptual_turning_points.initial_question: How is capitulum phenotype diversity distributed across geography and environment?
conceptual_turning_points.result: Different capitulum dimensions map to different environmental axes; one whole-capitulum ecological syndrome is insufficient.

conceptual_turning_points.initial_question: When did capitulum components change and what historical environmental triggers caused them?
conceptual_turning_points.result: Multiple components changed repeatedly at unequal evolutionary depths and without robust shared transition localization.

conceptual_turning_points.initial_question: How deep in time are the transitions?
conceptual_turning_points.result: The young age of the radiation makes the density of repeated phenotypic change itself the more surprising phenomenon.

conceptual_turning_points.initial_question: Can a recurring coarse climate or sea-level trigger explain the repeated changes?
conceptual_turning_points.result: No recurring coarse tested historical trigger is identified under current public-data uncertainty.

conceptual_turning_points.initial_question: What made repeated phenotypic innovation possible?
conceptual_turning_points.result: Test whether rapid capitulum diversification was fueled by reuse, sorting, exchange or regulatory deployment of pre-existing genomic variation rather than repeated de novo invention.

nature_scale_question: Why could a young thistle radiation repeatedly generate so much reproductive-phenotype diversity in so little evolutionary time?
high_risk_working_hypothesis: The radiation inherited, exchanged and recombined a reusable genomic toolkit, allowing capitulum components to be repeatedly reassembled instead of reinvented de novo.
claim_boundaries: The Japanese Cirsium radiation is not yet demonstrated to be an adaptive radiation.
Reticulation is not yet shown to cause capitulum diversity or species richness.
Standing variation is not yet shown to cause repeated capitulum states.
Phenotypic mosaicism is not proof of genetic or developmental modularity.
Ploidy is not yet shown to increase evolvability.
No capitulum trait is assumed to share the same genomic architecture as another.
Repeated phenotypes are not assumed to be adaptive.
design_implication: Prioritize populations and phenotype contrasts that discriminate among de novo mutation, ancestral standing variation, introgression and polyploid/regulatory reuse, with same-individual phenotype, DNA, cytotype and voucher linkage.
stop_rule: If a planned analysis cannot materially increase or decrease confidence in the source-of-evolvability hypotheses, it is peripheral to the Nature-scale aza3 programme.
